# Schedule Planner

A small course scheduling page. You add courses, it lays out your week in a grid, totals your
units, and warns you when two courses overlap.

There is no backend, no database, and no build step. It is three files: `index.html`,
`styles.css`, and `app.js`.

## Running it

Right now you can just open `index.html` in a browser. Double-clicking the file works.

**That stops working once you convert the code to ES modules,** which the assignment asks you to
do. Browsers refuse to load module imports from a `file://` address, and the page will come up
blank with a CORS error in the console. When you hit that, serve the folder over HTTP instead:

```
python -m http.server 8000
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000`. You already have Python from earlier in the course.

On Windows, if that command opens the Microsoft Store or says Python was not found, use `py`
instead:

```
py -m http.server 8000
```

Leave the command running in a terminal while you work, and restart it if you move files around.

## What it is supposed to do

This section is the specification. **If the code and this README disagree about what should
happen, this README is correct.** Read it carefully before you write tests, because a test is
only as good as your understanding of what the right answer was.

### Times

- Times are stored in 24-hour form as `"HH:MM"` strings, such as `"14:50"`.
- Times are displayed to the user in 12-hour form with AM or PM. `"09:00"` displays as
  `9:00 AM`, `"14:50"` displays as `2:50 PM`, `"12:00"` displays as `12:00 PM`, and `"00:30"`
  displays as `12:30 AM`.
- A course's end time must be later than its start time.

### Conflicts

Checked when you add a course. A new course conflicts with an existing one when **both** of these
are true:

- They meet on at least one of the same days.
- Their meeting times overlap.

Two rules that follow from that and are easy to get wrong:

- **Back-to-back courses do not conflict.** A course ending at 10:20 and a course starting at
  10:20 are fine together. They do not overlap; they touch.
- **Courses on different days never conflict,** no matter what time they meet.

### Units

- Units must be a whole number from 1 to 99. Anything else is rejected with a message.
- The unit total covers **every** course you have added, not just the ones currently matching the
  filter box. It appears both in the top bar and under the course list.
- A total above 54 units is flagged as needing approval. 54 itself is fine.

### The week grid

- Covers 8 am to 8 pm, Monday through Friday.
- A course appears as a block in every column for a day it meets, positioned and sized by its
  start and end times.
- Each block shows the course number and its start time.
- A course scheduled outside the 8 am to 8 pm window still appears in the course list, but its
  block is clamped to the top of the grid.

### Filtering

- Matches against the course number or the course title.
- Case-insensitive, so `calc` finds `Differential Calculus`.
- An empty filter box shows every course.
- Filtering changes which rows and blocks are listed, never the unit total.

### Required fields

- Course number and title are both required.
- At least one meeting day must be checked.

## Notes on the code

Three things about how this is written, because they will matter in Step 2 of the assignment:

- **The logic is tangled up with the page.** Time conversion, conflict detection, 12-hour
  formatting, validation, and unit totaling are all written inline inside `addCourse()`,
  `renderRoster()`, and `renderWeek()`, mixed in with `document.getElementById` calls. None of it
  can be called on its own right now, which is the problem the assignment opens with.
- **Some of it is written more than once.** Converting `"HH:MM"` into minutes happens in three
  separate places, and the 12-hour display formatting happens in two. If you ever need to change
  how one of those behaves, you currently have to find every copy. Pulling each into a single
  function is most of Step 2.
- **It uses inline `onclick` handlers,** both in `index.html` and in the HTML that
  `renderRoster()` builds for the remove buttons. These depend on the functions being global.
  When you switch to modules they will stop working silently, including the one inside the
  generated table rows. That one is the least obvious, so look for it.

This is roughly what a lot of working code looks like before anyone tries to test it. It is not
written badly on purpose, but it is not written with testing in mind either.
